# Review phase over several repos: validation gate and fixer

## What to build

Today `runReviewPhase` (`src/review/phase.ts`) works on exactly one repo: one `repo`, one `integrationWorktree`, one `integrationBranch`, one `startingCommit`, one `config.validate`. A multi-repo suite (a frontend and a backend in two git repos) needs one review phase over all of them. This task makes the **validation gate and the fixer** work over several repos; the reviewers (code reviewer, live tester) are a later task and keep working on the first repo only for now.

Add an optional `repos?: ReviewRepo[]` and `workspace?: string` to `ReviewPhaseOptions`. When `repos` is absent (every plain run, and today's suite), behavior is exactly as today: an internal helper builds a one-entry list from the legacy fields. When `repos` has several entries, `workspace` is a folder that holds each repo's integration worktree as a subfolder named after the repo (`<workspace>/<name>/`), and:

- **Gate and fix-pass validation** run each repo's own `config.validate` in that repo's worktree, with that repo's `validateParallel`. The first failing repo's result goes to the fixer.
- **The fixer** runs once, with cwd `workspace`, so it sees every repo. After it exits, the tool commits leftovers in **each** repo worktree that changed (`commitLeftovers`), the attempt succeeds if **at least one** repo got a new commit, a retry `resetHard`s **every** repo to its own start head, and the summary is the `git log` of every repo that changed.
- **Resume** of an interrupted fix pass resets every repo to its own saved base.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/review/phase.ts` (lines 41–69) — `ReviewPhaseOptions`; add `repos`/`workspace` here
- `src/review/phase.ts` (lines 93–98) — `trackChanges`: the live change view of a fixer; single-repo only
- `src/review/phase.ts` (lines 100–261) — the phase loop; `revParse(opts.repo, opts.integrationBranch)` at lines 170, 193, 238 saves `fixBase`
- `src/review/phase.ts` (lines 481–568) — `fixPass`: resume reset (492–497), the fixer options (499–514), validation loop (535–563)
- `src/review/phase.ts` (lines 579–643) — `gate`: the validation gate before round 0 and its fixer call
- `src/agents/fixer.ts` (lines 19–56) — `FixerOptions` / `FixerResult`
- `src/agents/fixer.ts` (lines 216–291) — `runFixer`: `before`, `commitLeftovers`, `hasNewCommit`, `resetHard`, summary from `git log`
- `src/state/state.ts` (lines 38–55) — `reviewStateSchema`: `fixBase` is one string today
- `src/validate/commands.ts` — `runCommands(commands, cwd, signal, { parallel })` and its result `{ ok, command, exitCode, ... }`
- `src/config/config.ts` (lines 8–39) — `Config`: `validate`, `validateParallel`, `setup`
- `src/providers/fake.ts` (lines 22–50, 93–152) — the fake provider: writes `write` files relative to `opts.cwd`, then `git add -A && git commit` in `opts.cwd`
- `src/review/phase-fix-pass.test.ts` — closest existing tests of the fix pass with the fake provider; mirror its setup
- `src/__fixtures__/repo.ts` — `tempRepo()`, `gitOut()`

## Patterns to follow

**Options with JSDoc, optional fields spread in:**
```ts
// src/review/phase.ts:55
/** The run's integration-worktree lock, held by the fixer while it works there. */
withLock?: MergeLock;
```

**The new type (export it from `src/review/phase.ts`):**
```ts
/** One repo of a multi-repo review phase (a suite whose features live in several repos). */
export interface ReviewRepo {
  /** Its folder name in `workspace`, also the prefix of its paths in prompts and logs. */
  name: string;
  /** Git root. */
  repo: string;
  integrationWorktree: string;
  integrationBranch: string;
  startingCommit: string;
  /** That repo's own config: `validate`, `validateParallel`, `setup`. */
  config: Config;
}
```
and an internal `const reposOf = (opts: ReviewPhaseOptions): ReviewRepo[] => opts.repos ?? [{ name: "", repo: opts.repo, integrationWorktree: opts.integrationWorktree, integrationBranch: opts.integrationBranch, startingCommit: opts.startingCommit, config: opts.config }]`. Suite-wide settings (`attempts`, `validationRounds`, `fixPasses`, `e2eReview`, `loopDetection`) still come from `opts.config`.

**Failure classes in retries:**
```ts
// src/agents/fixer.ts:246
return { ok: false, reason: { class: "no_commit", message: "the fixer made no commit" } };
```

**Test pattern:** tests build temp repos with `tempRepo()`, run `runReviewPhase` with `createFakeProvider(script)` from `src/providers/fake.ts`, and assert on git (`gitOut(repo, ["log", ...])`) and the result's `exitCode`.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `src/state/state.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `reviewStateSchema`, add `fixBases: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional()` with JSDoc "Per repo name, its integration head when fix pass `round` started (multi-repo review phase); `fixBase` keeps the first repo's." Keep `fixBase`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### UPDATE `src/agents/fixer.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `repos?: readonly { name: string; worktree: string }[]` to `FixerOptions` (JSDoc: "Several repos: `integrationWorktree` is then the workspace holding them, the agent's cwd; commits, leftovers and retries are per repo"). In `runFixer`, when `repos` has more than one entry:
  - `before` becomes a `Map<name, head>` from `currentHead(worktree)` for each repo; `dirtyAtStart` per repo.
  - `checkAttempt`: on exit 0, `commitLeftovers` in each repo (message unchanged), then succeed when `hasNewCommit` is true for at least one repo, else `no_commit` with message `the fixer made no commit in any repo`.
  - `prepare` on attempt > 1: `resetHard(worktree, before.get(name))` for each repo.
  - The summary: for each repo with new commits, `## <name>\n` + `git log --format=%B <before>..HEAD` in that worktree, joined by a blank line.
  - `FixerResult` gains `commits?: Record<string, string>` (new head per repo that changed); `commit` is the first changed repo's head.
  - Do not call `onAgentStart`/`onAgentEnd` in multi-repo mode (the live change view is per worktree; a later task handles the page).
  - The single-repo path must stay byte-for-byte the same in behavior.
- **IMPLEMENT**: the prompt (`fixerPrompt`) gains one line when `repos` is set: ``- Your folder holds several git repos: ${names}. Each is a separate repo; commit in the repo you changed.``
- **GOTCHA**: `withLock` is held for the whole run, as today. `integrationWorktree` (the workspace) is not a git repo: never run git in it.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/agents`

### UPDATE `src/review/phase.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `ReviewRepo`, `repos?: ReviewRepo[]` and `workspace?: string` on `ReviewPhaseOptions` (JSDoc: "Several repos (a multi-repo suite); the legacy single-repo fields are ignored for validation and fixing when set. `workspace` holds each repo's integration worktree as `<workspace>/<name>`.").
- **IMPLEMENT**: a helper `validateRepos(opts, signal)` that runs, for each repo of `reposOf(opts)` with a non-empty `config.validate`, `runCommands(r.config.validate, r.integrationWorktree, signal, { parallel: r.config.validateParallel })`, and returns the first failing result with its `command` rewritten to `[<name>] <command>` in multi-repo mode (unchanged with one repo), or `{ ok: true }`. Use it in `gate` (line 599) and in `fixPass` (line 548). The "no validate commands at all" early return in `gate` (line 582) and `fixPass` (line 535) checks every repo's list.
- **IMPLEMENT**: the fixer's `checks` are every repo's commands, prefixed `[<name>] ` in multi-repo mode; `integrationWorktree` passed to `runFixer` is `opts.workspace` and `repos` is `reposOf(opts).map((r) => ({ name: r.name, worktree: r.integrationWorktree }))` in multi-repo mode.
- **IMPLEMENT**: where `fixBase` is saved (lines 170, 238), also save `fixBases` (each repo's `revParse(r.repo, r.integrationBranch)`) in multi-repo mode. In `fixPass`'s resume reset (492–497) and `gate`'s reset (587), reset each repo's worktree (to its `fixBases[name]` / its current head).
- **IMPLEMENT**: `trackChanges` is only spread into the fixer options with one repo.
- **IMPLEMENT**: log lines that name `opts.integrationBranch` keep it (it is the same `suite/<id>` name in every repo).
- **GOTCHA**: `config.validate` of `opts.config` must no longer be used for validation in multi-repo mode; each repo's own config is.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/review`

### UPDATE `src/providers/fake.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: when `opts.cwd` is not inside a git work tree (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails), the default write (`<label>.txt` when `write` is absent) goes into the alphabetically first subfolder that is a git work tree, and the `commit` step runs `git add -A && git commit --allow-empty` in **every** subfolder that is a git work tree and has changes (skip clean ones; skip the commit entirely when none changed). Explicit `write` keys stay relative to `opts.cwd` (e.g. `"backend/x.txt"`). Document this next to `write` in `attemptSchema`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers`

### CREATE `src/review/phase-multi-repo.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: two temp repos `a` and `b` (`tempRepo()`), each with a branch `suite/x` and a worktree of it inside one temp `workspace` folder as `workspace/a` and `workspace/b` (`git worktree add`). Tests, all with `validateOnly: true` or with a fake script driving one fix pass:
  1. Repo `a` has `validate: ["node -e \"require('fs').writeFileSync('ran-a','')\""]`, repo `b` has none: after the gate, `workspace/a/ran-a` exists and `workspace/b/ran-a` does not.
  2. Repo `b`'s validate fails once (`test -f fixed.txt`) and the fake fixer writes `b/fixed.txt`: the gate passes after one validation fix round, `b`'s `suite/x` has one new commit, `a`'s `suite/x` is unchanged.
  3. A fixer attempt that writes nothing fails with `no_commit` and is retried; both repos are reset to their start heads between attempts.
  4. With no `repos`, an existing single-repo call behaves as before (reuse one existing case from `phase-fix-pass.test.ts`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/review/phase-multi-repo.test.ts`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `runReviewPhase` without `repos` behaves exactly as before: every existing test in `src/review`, `src/runner`, `src/suite` passes unchanged
- [ ] With two repos, each repo's `validate` runs only in its own worktree
- [ ] A failing validation in one repo goes to the fixer as `[<name>] <command>` and the fixer runs with cwd `workspace`
- [ ] The fixer's changes are committed in the repo they were made in only
- [ ] A retry or a resumed fix pass resets every repo to its own base
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint .`, `npx vitest run src/review src/agents src/providers` pass

## Validation commands

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint .
npx vitest run src/review src/agents src/providers
npx vitest run
```
